app.title: Digital Twin — Endurance: training-load model and its out-of-sample evidence
app.summary: A person opens a dashboard over training sessions that have already been processed, checks the data-source banner in the sidebar, and sets the two time constants of the fitness-fatigue load model. They read the daily load curves and the acute:chronic load ratio against its safety threshold, then a rolling-best performance envelope per sport with an adjustable window. They check the computed load score against an external implementation and browse the session table. They then rank model variants by out-of-sample R² against baselines and work through tabs of saved evaluation results: which capabilities the history supports yet, paired skill gains with intervals, detectability floors, replication across a cohort of athletes, hierarchical pooling, safety-rule checks and responder predictors. What they get is a judgement of what the load model can and cannot claim, and for whom.

task.text: Judge whether a training-load model really predicts an athlete's performance out of sample, and how far that holds across a cohort, before it is trusted for planning.

data.text: Processed endurance training sessions with daily load and performance observations, plus saved evaluation tables (cross-validation scores, paired bootstrap comparisons, cohort replication, posterior summaries).
data.item: a training session of one athlete, rolled up into a daily load and a performance observation

stage.text: validating a load model on processed training histories, after ingestion and before planning

mechanism.text: A sidebar picks one of five pages and sets the model's time constants, which recompute the load curves and the variant scores shown on the pages. Each page puts headline numbers above line, scatter or bar charts and tables, and the Measures page splits saved evaluation artifacts into tabs; an artifact that is missing shows the command that produces it instead of a chart.

field.text: fitness-fatigue training-load modelling with out-of-sample validation in sports science

workflow.name: judge whether a model predicts out of sample, against baselines

steps.here: reads the processed session, daily-load and performance artifacts, falling back to a frozen demo snapshot; the sidebar banner says whether the sources are real, and an empty store shows the commands to run
two sliders set the fitness and fatigue time constants in days; fitness must be longer than fatigue or the page stops

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: exponential moving averages of daily TRIMP give fitness, fatigue and freshness, and a 7-day/28-day acute:chronic ratio is drawn against its upper bound

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: per-session best efforts are plotted as dots under a rolling-maximum envelope whose window is set by a slider, in a running tab and a cycling-power tab, with lag-1 autocorrelation

steps.step: check the measure against an external reference
steps.here: the computed TRIMP is regressed on an external tool's TRIMP (slope, intercept, residual SD) over an identity line, above a session table sorted newest first
model variants and declared baselines are ranked by out-of-sample R² next to in-sample R² and their gap, for a chosen target

tabs of saved results: a capability ladder, paired skill gains with 95% intervals, detectability floors, a per-athlete forest plot across the cohort, pooled posterior estimates, and safety-rule and responder verdicts

distinctive: Every variant is ranked by its out-of-sample score against baselines declared in advance, including persistence (repeating the last value), and never by its fit.
A missing evaluation artifact is shown as the command that produces it, not as an empty chart, and a provenance banner flags whether any data is synthetic.
Performance is a rolling-best envelope over a window rather than each session's effort, because single efforts are noise around a level.
Null results come with a detectability floor: a known effect is injected to show the smallest one the protocol could see.
A maturity ladder says which claims the athlete's history supports yet, and how many days or measurements each missing one still needs.
